test_title: PYST 38: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the threshold amount for complaints to be auto-converted into an e‑Zero FIR?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹10 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** has implemented a mechanism where financial fraud complaints reported on the **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCCRP)** involving an amount of **₹10 lakh** or more are automatically converted into an **e-Zero FIR**.
 
• This initiative is designed to ensure that **high-value financial frauds** are met with immediate legal action and formal investigation without the delay of jurisdictional disputes.
 
• The **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal** (www.cybercrime.gov.in) was launched in **2019** to allow victims to report all types of cybercrimes, especially those against women and children, and financial frauds.
 
• The **Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, manages the portal and coordinates with **States and Union Territories** to handle these complaints.
 
• The auto-conversion into an **e-Zero FIR** helps in the rapid tracking of the **money trail** across multiple bank accounts and states, increasing the chances of recovering the defrauded amount. ***Hence, the correct answer is ₹10 lakh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zero FIR:** 
 
 
• A **Zero FIR** is a First Information Report that can be filed in **any police station**, regardless of where the incident occurred.
 
• Unlike a regular FIR, it is given a **serial number '0'** (zero) and is later transferred to the police station that has the appropriate **jurisdiction** for investigation.
 
• This concept was introduced based on the recommendations of the **Justice Verma Committee** in **2013**, following the **Nirbhaya case**, to ensure that the police cannot refuse to register a complaint citing a lack of jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **Cyber Fraud Helpline:**
 
 
• The **National Helpline Number 1930** (formerly 155260) is dedicated to reporting online financial frauds.
 
• It works in tandem with the **Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS)** to provide immediate assistance.
 
 
 
• **I4C (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre):**
 
 
• Established in **2018**, it serves as a nodal point in the fight against **cybercrime** in India.
 
• It has several components including the **National Cyber Crime Threat Analytics Unit** and the **National Cyber Crime Forensic Laboratory**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **CFCFRMS System:** This system allows for the **real-time freezing** of funds. When a victim reports a fraud on **1930** or the portal, the **CFCFRMS** sends alerts to the respective **Banks** or **Wallets** to block the transaction before the fraudster can withdraw the money.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, which replaced the **CrPC**, has formalized the provisions for **Zero FIR** and **e-FIR**, making it mandatory for police stations to register them.
 
• **Data Fact:** Since its inception, the **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal** has helped in saving **hundreds of crores** of rupees of citizens' money by facilitating the prompt blocking of defrauded amounts.
 
• The threshold of **₹10 lakh** was specifically chosen to prioritize **major scams** that involve significant economic loss and complex **inter-state** criminal networks.
